newsitem.title: UK: UK MPs see cost bar to overseas pensioners' claim.
newsitem.headline: UK MPs see cost bar to overseas pensioners' claim.

text.p: A parliamentary committee on Wednesday dashed the hopes of nearly half a million British retirees overseas who have been campaigning for their state pensions to be increased in line with inflation.

Although Britain since 1955 has paid state pensions to its citizens anywhere in the world, it has paid cost-of-living rises only to pensioners in countries that have signed bilateral agreements to that end with London.
As a result, an estimated 433,000 pensioners -- most of them in Australia and Canada -- receive only token pensions.

For example, a person who retired overseas in 1966 on a full pension of four pounds ($6.40) a week still receives the same amount -- unless they have been living in the European Economic Area, the U.S. or a handful of other countries.

Successive governments have baulked at paying the cost, estimated at 235 million pounds a year, of uprating the "frozen" pensions -- a stance that parliament's Social Security Committee implicitly endorsed in a report on Wednesday.

"Given the perennial constraints on public expenditure, it is hard to identify a single compromise which would substantially meet the expatriate pensioners' case at a reasonable cost," the cross-party committee said.

The MPs, who heard first hand in December of the anger that expatriate pensioners felt at being deprived of a full pension, said it was not a question of reaching a moral judgement and then deciding whether the country could afford to pay more.
The question was essentially a political one, the MPs said.

"Ultimately, it must be for the House (of Commons) to decide, and that is our concluding recommendation: that there should be a free vote at prime time to allow Members (of Parliament) to express their opinion..." the report said. ($1=.6237 Pound)
